intro: Listen to an announcement in a physiology lab.
text: Before we begin today's blood pressure lab, a change to the procedure. Originally, you were going to measure each other before and after climbing the stairs in the east stairwell, but that stairwell is closed for repairs, so instead, you'll do two minutes of step exercise on the platforms by the window. Record three readings: at rest, right after exercise, and five minutes later. Anyone with a heart condition or high blood pressure should be the recorder, not the subject, for this lab. And if a reading looks unusually high, stop and call me over rather than repeating it yourself.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce that the east stairwell has reopened
To explain a modified lab procedure and safety rules
To teach students how a blood pressure cuff measures readings
To assign partners for the blood pressure lab
questions.explanation: The coordinator explains the new step exercise, the readings to record, and who should not be tested.

questions.prompt: What should students do if they get an unusually high reading?
options: Repeat the measurement after five minutes of rest
Switch roles so the subject becomes the recorder
Ask the lab coordinator to come and check it
Do two more minutes of step exercise and remeasure
questions.explanation: She tells students to stop and call her over rather than repeating an unusually high reading themselves.

intro: Listen to an announcement in a landscape architecture class.
text: About Friday's site visit to Corliss Park. The city planning office originally planned to meet us at the park's main entrance, but since the north meadow is the area you'll be redesigning, we'll meet at the meadow parking lot off Route Nine instead, at two thirty. Bring measuring tapes and the base map I handed out. If it's raining, we'll still go, but we'll spend the first hour in the park's visitor center, going over the drainage plans with the city engineer. Your site analysis is due in two weeks, and the city will review the three strongest proposals.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce a design competition run by the city
To explain how to draw a map of the north meadow
To give updated details about a site visit
To introduce the engineer who designed the park
questions.explanation: The professor explains the new meeting place for the site visit and what will happen there.

questions.prompt: What will happen if it rains on Friday?
options: The group will start with an hour indoors on drainage plans
The visit will be moved to the following week instead
The group will meet at the park's main entrance instead of the lot
The site analysis will be due later than two weeks
questions.explanation: The professor says that if it rains they will still go but spend the first hour in the visitor center on drainage plans.

intro: Listen to an announcement at the campus library.
text: Hello, everyone. Some changes to the Special Collections reading room on the library's fifth floor. Starting next month, it'll be open by appointment only, rather than for walk-ins, and appointments must be made at least two days in advance. Hours are also changing: instead of nine to five, the room will be open ten to four, Monday through Thursday. As before, only pencils are allowed, and bags go in the lockers outside. Faculty bringing an entire class may still book evening sessions, but only if they request them a full two weeks ahead.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce new access rules for a library reading room
To introduce a new collection of rare books
To explain how students can rent lockers outside the reading room
To invite faculty to give evening lectures
questions.explanation: The librarian explains that the reading room will require appointments and will have shorter hours.

questions.prompt: A student wants to visit on a Thursday at three p.m. What must the student do?
options: Request an evening session two weeks ahead
Arrive before the room closes at five
Ask a professor to bring a whole class
Make an appointment by the Tuesday before
questions.explanation: Appointments must be made at least two days in advance, so a Thursday visit needs to be booked by Tuesday.

intro: Listen to an announcement at a residence hall meeting.
text: Good evening. This year's room selection process is changing. Instead of choosing rooms in order of class year, everyone will receive a random lottery number on March third. To be included, you must pay a two-hundred-dollar deposit by February twentieth, which counts toward next year's rent. Students who want to keep their current room can skip the lottery, unless they live in Harper Hall, which is being converted to first-year housing. Selection days run March tenth through the twelfth, and if you're studying abroad, a friend may choose for you, with your written permission.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To explain a new process for selecting housing
To announce higher rent for next year's housing
To recruit students to study abroad next year
To describe the renovation of Harper Hall
questions.explanation: The director explains that rooms will now be assigned through a lottery and describes the deadlines and exceptions.

questions.prompt: What is true about students who currently live in Harper Hall?
options: They will receive lottery numbers before March third
They do not need to pay the two-hundred-dollar deposit
They will choose rooms by class year as before
They cannot keep their current rooms next year
questions.explanation: Harper Hall is becoming first-year housing, so its current residents cannot skip the lottery to keep their rooms.

intro: Listen to an announcement on the campus radio station.
text: Good morning. This is Campus Transit. Starting Monday, the Green Line will no longer stop at Fairview Apartments. Instead, it'll run directly between the library and the medical campus every ten minutes, rather than every twenty. Fairview residents should use the new Orange Line, which leaves from the apartment entrance on the hour and half hour. Both lines are free with a student ID, except that after nine p.m., the Orange Line becomes an on-demand service, which you'll need to request through the campus app. Updated maps are posted at every stop and online.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To explain how to download the campus app
To announce a new bus fare for riders who don't have a student ID
To announce changes to campus bus routes and service
To warn about delays near the medical campus
questions.explanation: The director describes the Green Line's new route and the new Orange Line for Fairview residents.

questions.prompt: How can a Fairview resident get a bus at ten p.m.?
options: By requesting a ride through the campus app
By catching the Green Line at the library
By waiting at the entrance on the half hour
By showing a student ID at the bus stop
questions.explanation: After nine p.m., the Orange Line becomes on-demand and must be requested through the campus app.

intro: Listen to an announcement on the campus radio station.
text: Hi, everyone. Plans for Saturday's homecoming parade have changed. Because of construction on College Avenue, the route will now start at the north end of Maple Street and finish at the stadium, instead of going through downtown. Lineup for floats begins at eight thirty, and the parade starts at ten. Student groups entering a float must register by Wednesday, and floats can be no wider than ten feet, so they'll fit through the stadium gate. Parking on Maple Street is prohibited from seven to noon, except for residents with permits; any other cars will be towed.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To describe changes to the homecoming parade
To announce construction work on College Avenue
To recruit student groups to build parade floats
To explain new parking permits for residents
questions.explanation: The coordinator explains the parade's new route and the rules for floats and parking.

questions.prompt: Whose car can stay parked on Maple Street on Saturday morning?
options: A student's car parked there before seven
A car belonging to a float's driver
A resident's car that displays a permit
Any car that is moved again by ten
questions.explanation: Parking on Maple Street is banned from seven to noon except for residents with permits.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the campus facilities office.
text: This is an important message from Facilities. Power to the Science Quad, including Baxter, Lund, and Reyes Halls, will be shut off this Sunday from six a.m. to two p.m. while we replace a transformer. This work was originally scheduled for next month, but last week's storm damaged the equipment. All three buildings will be locked. Researchers with freezers or incubators should move samples to the backup cold room in the Medical Sciences Building, which will stay powered. Anyone who can't move their materials by Saturday at five should contact our office about a portable generator.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To report damage caused by last week's storm
To announce a new cold room in Medical Sciences
To warn about a power shutdown and explain what to do
To explain why the Science Quad buildings are being rebuilt
questions.explanation: The director announces Sunday's power shutdown and tells researchers how to protect their samples.

questions.prompt: What should a researcher who cannot move samples by Saturday evening do?
options: Leave the samples in Reyes Hall until two p.m.
Move them to the cold room on Sunday morning
Wait until the work is done next month
Contact the facilities office about a generator
questions.explanation: Anyone unable to move materials by Saturday at five should contact Facilities about a portable generator.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the campus career center.
text: Hi, everyone. The career center's annual headshot day is this Thursday. We originally planned to hold it in our office, but since we're expecting more than two hundred students, we've moved it to the Commons Ballroom. Photos are free and take about five minutes, and you'll receive your digital photo by email within three business days. Walk-ins are welcome from ten to two. However, if you also want a résumé review, book an appointment online, because advisors will be there only from two to four. Please dress as you would for an interview.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To explain how to dress for a job interview
To give updated information about a career center event
To announce a new fee for professional photos
To recruit volunteer advisors to review students' résumés
questions.explanation: The director announces the new location of headshot day and explains walk-in hours and résumé reviews.

questions.prompt: A student wants both a photo and a résumé review. What should the student do?
options: Walk in to the career center office at ten
Arrive at the ballroom before two without booking
Book an online appointment for the afternoon
Email an advisor within three business days
questions.explanation: Résumé reviews require an online appointment because advisors are present only from two to four.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the campus counseling center.
text: Hello. This is a message from the counseling center. Starting next week, we're replacing our Friday walk-in hours with daily drop-in sessions, Monday through Friday, from one to three. Each drop-in visit lasts about twenty minutes and is meant for short-term concerns. If you'd like ongoing support, you'll still need to schedule an intake appointment, which now happens over the phone instead of in person. All services are free for enrolled students. And if you're facing an urgent situation outside these hours, call our after-hours line rather than waiting for the next drop-in session.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To advertise a new after-hours phone line
To explain a new fee for ongoing counseling appointments
To announce changes to counseling center services
To recruit students for a support group
questions.explanation: The director explains the new daily drop-in sessions and how intake appointments now work.

questions.prompt: What should a student who wants regular, ongoing counseling do first?
options: Schedule an intake appointment by phone
Visit a drop-in session on Friday afternoon
Call the after-hours line in the evening
Come to the center in person for intake
questions.explanation: Ongoing support requires an intake appointment, which now happens over the phone.

intro: Listen to an announcement at the campus recreation center.
text: Good afternoon. The annual Campus Fun Run is happening next Sunday, but there's been a change: the course is now five kilometers rather than ten, because part of the river path is flooded. Check-in opens at the north end of the stadium at seven thirty, and the race starts at eight thirty sharp. Registration is fifteen dollars and includes a T-shirt, but only if you register by Wednesday; after that, it's twenty dollars, and shirts aren't guaranteed. All proceeds go to the campus food pantry. Runners with strollers or dogs should start at the back of the group.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To warn students about flooding on the river path
To give updated details about a charity run
To ask for donations to the campus food pantry
To recruit volunteers to staff the check-in table
questions.explanation: The director explains the shortened course and the check-in times and registration fees for the run.

questions.prompt: What will a runner who registers on Friday probably get?
options: A T-shirt and entry for fifteen dollars
A starting spot at the front of the group at eight thirty
Entry into the original ten-kilometer race
Entry for twenty dollars, possibly without a shirt
questions.explanation: After Wednesday, registration costs twenty dollars and T-shirts are not guaranteed.

intro: Listen to an announcement at a campus literary event.
text: Good evening, everyone. I'm excited to announce that novelist Daniel Asante will give a reading on campus on October ninth. We'd planned to hold it in the Wren Library lounge, but with more than three hundred people registered, it's moving to Marlow Theater, which seats five hundred. The reading starts at seven, followed by a book signing at eight thirty. Copies of his new novel will be sold at the door for eighteen dollars. Admission is free, but registration is still required, except for students in creative writing courses, who are automatically on the list.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To review the novelist's latest book
To sell tickets for a theater performance
To announce a change of location for an author event
To invite students to join a new creative writing course
questions.explanation: The coordinator announces that the reading has moved to Marlow Theater and gives details about the event.

questions.prompt: Who does NOT need to register for the reading?
options: Anyone who buys a copy of the novel
People who plan to stay for the signing
Those who arrive after seven o'clock
Students taking creative writing courses
questions.explanation: Registration is required except for students in creative writing courses, who are automatically on the list.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the campus tutoring center.
text: Hi, everyone. Some news from the Tutoring Center. The Math Help Room is moving from the basement of Pell Hall to Room 210 in the new Learning Commons. Because of the move, it'll be closed this Thursday and Friday, and it reopens on Monday with longer hours, nine a.m. to nine p.m. Tutors cover all courses up to Calculus Three. Most help is drop-in, but for courses above that level, you'll need to request an appointment at least a day ahead, so we can find a qualified tutor. Bring your textbook and the specific problems you're stuck on.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce the move and new schedule of a tutoring service
To recruit tutors for advanced math courses
To introduce the new Learning Commons building
To explain changes to the Calculus Three course and its tutors
questions.explanation: The director announces the Math Help Room's new location, closure dates, and longer hours.

questions.prompt: What should a student in a course beyond Calculus Three do to get help?
options: Drop in at Room 210 any time before nine p.m.
Visit Pell Hall on Thursday or Friday this week
Request an appointment at least a day in advance
Bring a textbook to the basement of Pell Hall
questions.explanation: Courses above Calculus Three require an appointment requested at least a day ahead.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the financial aid office.
text: Hello, everyone. The financial aid office is holding a workshop on completing next year's aid application. We'd scheduled just one session, on January twentieth, but since it filled within a day, we've added a second on the twenty-seventh, both from five to seven in Room 101 of Ashford Hall. Bring your family's tax information from last year. The priority deadline is March first; applications after that are still accepted, but only for loans, not grants. Parents who can't attend in person may join by video, as long as you let us know in advance.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To explain how to file family tax returns
To announce a new grant program for students starting in March
To announce workshops on applying for financial aid
To remind students that loans must be repaid
questions.explanation: The counselor announces two workshop sessions for completing the aid application and explains the deadline.

questions.prompt: What would a student who applies on March tenth probably be eligible for?
options: Grants, but not loans
Both grants and loans
Neither grants nor loans
Loans, but not grants
questions.explanation: Applications after the March first deadline are accepted only for loans, not grants.

intro: Listen to an announcement from the registrar's office.
text: Attention, graduating seniors. Commencement tickets will be handed out at the registrar's office in Bishop Hall from May first through the fifth. Each graduate receives four guest tickets, down from the six we originally announced, because the ceremony has moved indoors to Carlton Arena after the stadium renovation fell behind schedule. You must pick up your tickets in person with your student ID; friends can't collect them for you, unless you submit a signed form beforehand. Extra tickets may become available on May eighth, but only if other graduates return ones they won't use.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce the completion of the stadium renovation
To invite seniors to a graduation party in Bishop Hall
To ask graduates to return all of their unused tickets by May eighth
To explain how and when graduates can get ceremony tickets
questions.explanation: The registrar explains the dates, location, and rules for picking up commencement tickets.

questions.prompt: How might a graduate get more than four tickets?
options: By being the first to pick up tickets in person on May first
By getting extras that others return, on May eighth
By submitting a signed form to the registrar
By attending the outdoor stadium ceremony
questions.explanation: Extra tickets may become available on May eighth if other graduates return unused ones.

intro: Listen to an announcement at the campus makerspace.
text: Hi, everyone. Some changes at the Makerspace in the basement of Dunn Library. Because demand for our 3D printers has doubled, print jobs are now limited to six hours each, down from twelve. Material is free for jobs under fifty grams; larger jobs cost ten cents a gram, charged to your student account. We're also closing on Sundays, but staying open until midnight Monday through Thursday. Before using any printer, you need to complete the one-hour safety training, unless you already took it last year, in which case a short online refresher is enough.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To announce the purchase of new 3D printers
To explain new policies at a campus makerspace
To recruit students to teach safety training
To explain how to design objects for printing
questions.explanation: The coordinator explains new limits on print jobs, material fees, hours, and training requirements.

questions.prompt: What does a student who completed the safety training last year need to do?
options: Retake the one-hour training in person
Pay ten cents a gram for the refresher
Complete a short online refresher course
Nothing, since last year's training counts
questions.explanation: Students who took the training last year only need a short online refresher.
